MOON-SITE-01.name: LROC Anthropogenic Objects
MOON-SITE-01.provider: LROC Science Operations Center, Arizona State University (NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter), via NASA PDS
MOON-SITE-01.licence: U.S. public domain (NASA PDS); credit requested
MOON-SITE-01.attribution: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University. Wagner, R. V. et al. (2017) Coordinates of anthropogenic features on the Moon. Icarus 283, 92-103, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.05.011
limitations: Only objects located in LROC NAC images are listed; Luna 9 and Luna 13 are added from NASA NSSDCA (MOON-SITE-01-SUPPLEMENT), while impact sites never seen from orbit (Luna 2, Ranger 4, SMART-1, Lunar Prospector, most LM ascent stages and spent stages) are not included.
DATE is documented as the arrival date, but for Luna 16, Luna 17, Luna 20, Luna 21, Luna 23, Luna 24 and Surveyor 1 it holds the launch date; affected rows carry a dateNote.
elevationM = RADIUS - 1 737 400 m: height above the reference sphere, not above a geoid or local terrain.
Coordinate uncertainty is LROC's own figure (metres); 0 m means a laser-ranging position.
kind is derived from LROC's OBJECT text by this project; heritage marks which NASA-2011 keep-out radius the backend draws (see MOON-SITE-06).
MOON-SITE-01.notes: 71 LROC rows (release of 2026-08-14) plus 2 supplement rows. Name = SHORT_NAME; VEHCL_NAME kept as `vehicle`.

MOON-SITE-01-SUPPLEMENT.name: Soft landings missing from the LROC list (supplement)
MOON-SITE-01-SUPPLEMENT.provider: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA)
MOON-SITE-01-SUPPLEMENT.attribution: NASA NSSDCA, D. R. Williams: Soviet Missions to the Moon; Surveyor missions
limitations: Reported landing positions (0.01° precision), not measured from orbit: the Luna 9 and Luna 13 landers have not been identified in LROC images, so their true positions may differ.

Added because CLAUDE-Moon-Data-Sources.md §9 (MOON-SITE-01 gotcha 3) lists them as missing; every §9 soft landing with a coordinate was found in the LROC file, so no catalogue coordinate had to be added.
MOON-SITE-01-SUPPLEMENT.notes: Rows: Luna9, Luna13. Landing dates (supplement rows and dateNotes) come from NASA NSSDCA: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunarussr.html, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1974-084A, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/surveyor.html.

MOON-PLACE-01.name: Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (Moon centre points)
MOON-PLACE-01.provider: IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature (WGPSN) / USGS Astrogeology Science Center
MOON-PLACE-01.licence: U.S. public domain (USGS); names are IAU-approved nomenclature
MOON-PLACE-01.attribution: Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Planetary Geomatics Group of the USGS Astrogeology Science Center, https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov. International Astronomical Union (IAU) Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature (WGPSN)
limitations: Centre points and nominal diameters only; names are labels, not surveyed boundaries.
The file is rebuilt nightly upstream; this copy is a snapshot at retrievedAt.
A diameter of 0 upstream (unknown, e.g. Statio landing-site names) is null here.
approved is the IAU approval year (the gazetteer stores most dates as 1 January of that year) or the full date when one is given.
A lettered crater's origin is null when it only repeats its parent crater's eponym; read it from the parent entry (same name without the letter).
MOON-PLACE-01.notes: Approved ('Adopted by IAU') names only; longitudes converted from 0-360 to ±180; coordinates rounded to 4 decimals (~3 m); diameters to 3 significant figures; id = USGS Feature ID; type = singular descriptor ('Crater, craters' -> 'Crater'; 'Satellite Feature' -> 'Lettered crater', the IAU's own definition of lunar satellite features); approved = IAU approval year, or full date when not 1 January. origin is null on 6999 lettered craters whose text repeats their parent crater's word for word (the parent entry keeps it), to keep the file under 2 MB.

MOON-PLACE-02.name: LROC global mare boundaries (65°S-65°N)
MOON-PLACE-02.provider: LROC Science Operations Center, Arizona State University (NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter), via NASA PDS
MOON-PLACE-02.licence: U.S. public domain (NASA PDS); credit requested
MOON-PLACE-02.attribution: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University. Nelson, D. M. et al. (2014) Mapping lunar maria extents and lobate scarps using LROC image products. LPSC 45, abstract 2861
limitations: Covers 65°S-65°N only: no mare outlines near the poles.

Digitised at 1:200,000-1:500,000 from WAC and Clementine mosaics, then simplified here (Douglas-Peucker 0.015° ≈ 455 m, coordinates snapped to 0.001°): use for context and cell lookup, not for boundaries.
Some names are LROC unit names rather than IAU features (e.g. 'Oceanus Procellarum - south', 'Cognitum East').
MOON-PLACE-02.notes: 644 polygons merged into 97 features by MARE_NAME; 7 self-intersecting polygons repaired (shapely make_valid); simplification tolerance 0.015°; areaKm2 = sum of the upstream AREA_KM values; diacritics lost in the DBF and two typos restored to IAU spelling.

MOON-SITE-02.name: Planned missions and Artemis candidate regions, 2027-2030 (curated)
MOON-SITE-02.provider: New Worlds project curation (CLAUDE-Moon-Data-Sources.md §9) from NASA, CNSA, ISRO, JAXA and company announcements
MOON-SITE-02.licence: Project compilation of public announcements (facts; no upstream licence)
MOON-SITE-02.attribution: Curated by the New Worlds project; Artemis regions: NASA (Oct 2024)
limitations: Announced plans as of 2026-11-08; dates slip often and targets change.
NASA published no polygons for the Artemis regions: each box is ~15 × 15 km centred on the anchor feature, while the real region sits on that feature's rim or flank.
Mission points are approximate (catalogue coordinates or gazetteer feature centres); missions without a published site have no geometry.
MOON-SITE-02.notes: url is NASA's Oct 2024 Artemis landing-regions update; mission rows follow the catalogue's §9 table.

MOON-SITE-06.name: NASA's Recommendations to Space-Faring Entities: How to Protect and Preserve the Historic and Scientific Value of U.S. Government Lunar Artifacts (Rev A)
MOON-SITE-06.attribution: NASA (2011), Recommendations to Space-Faring Entities, Rev A, 28 Oct 2011
limitations: Recommendations, not law: the document states it does not represent mandatory U.S. government or international requirements.
Written for U.S. government artifacts; this app applies the same radii to every nation's landing and impact sites as a modelling choice.
2.0 km around heritage landing and roving hardware and 0.5 km around heritage impact sites bound the descent/landing path; the Apollo 11 (75 m) and Apollo 17 (225 m) walking limits are not drawn.
Rings are centred on each site's recorded coordinate; experiments and retroreflectors get no ring of their own because they lie inside their lunar module's 2.0 km ring.
MOON-SITE-06.notes: Applied to sites whose heritage property is 'landing' or 'impact' in sites/anthropogenic_objects.geojson.
